label: TP
reason: User input from request parameters flows directly to bar via Base64 encode/decode cycle which preserves content. The returned bar is then passed to Utils.encodeForHTML and printed in HTML context. While encoding mitigates some XSS vectors, the CodeQL rule flags this pattern as vulnerable because certain payloads (like javascript:false encoded to javascript:false or other bypasses) might still render executable scripts depending on implementation specifics of the encoder used. Given the explicit warning about user-provided value reaching the sink, this is treated as a genuine potential XSS risk requiring review.

evidence.note: Parameter extracted from request flows through doSomething (which returns unchanged string after round-trip Base64) and is printed via encodeForHTML in HTML response.
